question: Walk me through the difference between GET, POST, PUT, and DELETE, and what a 404 versus a 500 status code tells the client.
idealAnswer:
GET retrieves a resource and should not change server state, POST creates a new resource or triggers an action, PUT replaces a resource entirely, DELETE removes it

Correctly distinguishes PUT (full replace, client sends the complete resource) from PATCH-like partial updates, even if PATCH itself isn't asked about directly

4xx codes mean the client did something wrong (404 means the requested resource doesn't exist, 400 means a malformed request), while 5xx codes mean the server failed while processing an otherwise valid request

A strong answer notes why this distinction matters practically: 4xx errors usually shouldn't be retried as-is, while 5xx errors might be transient and worth retrying

Mentions that status codes are a contract clients rely on, returning a 200 with an error message in the body instead of the right status code breaks that contract
